keyVerseText: All the best of the oil, and all the best of the wine, and of the wheat, the firstfruits of them which they shall offer unto the LORD, them have I given thee. best: Heb. fat
rootMeaning: The root of יִצְהָר (yitshâr) comes from צָהַר (tsâhar), which means 'to press out oil' or 'to glisten.' This root emphasizes the process of extracting fresh, shining oil, highlighting the purity and brightness inherent in the substance. Beyond the common English gloss of 'oil,' the root conveys the idea of something freshly produced and radiant, not merely any oil but one that reflects light and life.
usageInScripture: The word יִצְהָר appears 23 times in the Hebrew Bible, consistently referring to fresh, pure oil often associated with agricultural abundance and offerings to God. Its translations vary slightly—'and oil,' 'and the oil,' 'and thine oil'—but all maintain the connection to the best or firstfruits of the oil product. This suggests a consistent use emphasizing the value and purity of the oil as a gift or possession, often linked with other agricultural produce like wine and grain.
theologicalSignificance: Theologically, יִצְהָר carries rich meaning as it denotes not just any oil but the finest, freshly pressed oil that glistens with purity. This oil symbolizes God's provision and blessing, as it is often part of the firstfruits offered to the Lord. In the biblical context, oil also represents anointing, a divine setting apart for holy purposes, pointing forward to Christ as the Anointed One. Understanding יִצְהָר as both a physical substance and a symbol of consecration deepens our appreciation of God's generous and sanctifying work in the life of His people.
keyVerseReflection: Numbers 18:12 states, 'All the best of the oil, and all the best of the wine, and of the wheat, the firstfruits of them which they shall offer unto the LORD, them have I given thee.' The use of יִצְהָר here highlights that the oil is not ordinary but the 'best' or 'fat'—the choicest portion set apart for the Lord. This underscores the principle of offering God the finest of what He provides, reflecting a heart of worship and gratitude that recognizes God's provision and holiness.
